d: Example of how to create a simple frontend UI powered with TextChatService.
h:
When platform-integrated chat is enabled, custom UIs can no longer render player message text themselves. Use TextChannelWindow instead of reading Text or listening to MessageReceived for display.

This example shows how to use the TextChatService class to design your own frontend. It reuses the default text channels from CreateDefaultTextChannels and is very simple compared to the default UI.

  1. Disable the default UI that comes with the TextChatService by setting the ChatWindowConfiguration.Enabled and ChatInputBarConfiguration.Enabled properties to false in Studio's Properties window.

  2. Create a replacement for the chat input bar. This is the text box that emits messages when the user presses Enter.

  3. Create a ScreenGui and parent it to StarterGui.

  4. Create a TextBox and parent it to the new ScreenGui, then reposition and resize it as desired.
  5. Create a LocalScript and parent it to the new TextBox.

  6. Add the following code to the LocalScript:

        **Client**

    ```lua
    local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

    -- RBXGeneral is the default public channel
    local RBXGeneral = TextChatService:FindFirstChild("TextChannels"):WaitForChild("RBXGeneral")

    local textBox = script.Parent
    textBox.FocusLost:Connect(function(enterPressed)
        local text = textBox.Text
        if enterPressed and #text > 0 then
            local success, response = pcall(function()
                return RBXGeneral:SendAsync(textBox.Text)
            end)

            if not success then
                RBXGeneral:DisplaySystemMessage("Failed to send message")
            end

            -- Users expect the input box to be cleared after sending a message
            textBox.Text = ""
        end
    end)
    ```

  7. Create a replacement for the chat window. This is the ScrollingFrame that displays messages as they are received from TextChatService.MessageReceived. This step also creates a UIListLayout to automatically layout the messages.

  8. Create another new ScreenGui and parent it to StarterGui.

  9. Create a ScrollingFrame and parent it to the ScreenGui, then reposition and resize it as desired.
  10. Create a UIListLayout and parent it to the ScrollingFrame.
  11. Create a LocalScript and parent it to the ScrollingFrame.
  12. Add the following code to the LocalScript:
    **Client**

```lua
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

-- Function to create a new text label for each message received
local function addMessageGui(textChatMessage: TextChatMessage)
    local isOutgoingMessage = textChatMessage.Status == Enum.TextChatMessageStatus.Sending

    local parent = script.Parent

    local originalLabel = parent:FindFirstChild(textChatMessage.MessageId)
    if originalLabel then
        originalLabel.Text = textChatMessage.Text
        originalLabel.BackgroundTransparency = if isOutgoingMessage then 0.5 else 0
    else
        local textLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
        textLabel.BorderSizePixel = 0
        textLabel.Font = Enum.Font.BuilderSans
        textLabel.TextSize = 18
        textLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
        textLabel.BackgroundTransparency = if isOutgoingMessage then 0.5 else 0
        textLabel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0)
        textLabel.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
        textLabel.Name = textChatMessage.MessageId
        textLabel.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
        textLabel.Text = textChatMessage.Text
        textLabel.Parent = parent
    end
end

-- Start listening for incoming messages
TextChatService.MessageReceived:Connect(addMessageGui)
```

<div class="callout c-warning" markdown="1">
When using the TextChatService.MessageReceived event, it's important to check if the message already exists in the chat window. This event is called once when sending and once when the message is received from the server.
</div>
    1. Test your game by sending messages in the chat input bar. You should see the messages appear in the chat window. You can then expand on this example by adding features such as focusing the TextBox when a key is pressed or adding chat tags.

kid.simple: This example shows how to build your own simple chat box instead of using Roblox's default one. You turn off the default chat window and input bar, then make a TextBox for typing and a ScrollingFrame that lists messages. It helps you understand how chat messages are sent and received. Heads up: if platform-integrated chat is turned on, custom UIs can no longer show message text, so you would use a `TextChannelWindow` instead.
kid.analogy: It is like swapping the speaker and microphone on a walkie-talkie for your own. The radio signal (TextChatService) still carries the messages, you just built new parts to talk into and listen from.
keyPoints: First turn off the default UI by setting `ChatWindowConfiguration.Enabled` and `ChatInputBarConfiguration.Enabled` to false in the Properties window.
The input bar is a `TextBox` in a `ScreenGui` in StarterGui, with a LocalScript inside it.
When the player presses Enter, the script sends the text with `RBXGeneral:SendAsync()`, wrapped in `pcall` in case it fails.
After sending, clear the TextBox so it is ready for the next message.
The chat window is a `ScrollingFrame` with a `UIListLayout` that stacks a `TextLabel` for each message.
`TextChatService.MessageReceived` fires twice for your own message: once when sending and once when the server confirms it. Reuse the same label instead of making two.
With platform-integrated chat enabled, this approach stops working. Use `TextChannelWindow` instead.

terms.frontend: The part of a system that players see and touch, like buttons and text boxes.
terms.RBXGeneral: The default public chat channel that everyone in the server can see.
terms.SendAsync: A function that sends a message into a channel. Async means it may take a moment to finish.
terms.pcall: Short for protected call. It runs a function and catches errors, so one failure does not crash your whole script.
terms.FocusLost: An event that fires when the player stops typing in a TextBox, for example by pressing Enter or clicking away.
terms.MessageId: A unique name for each message. The example names each label with it so it can find and update the same label later.
terms.UIListLayout: An object that automatically lines up its siblings in a list, so you do not have to place each label by hand.

example.title: Send chat from your own TextBox
example.place: LocalScript inside a TextBox, inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui
example.code:
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

-- RBXGeneral is the default public channel
local channels = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels")
local general = channels:WaitForChild("RBXGeneral")

local textBox = script.Parent

textBox.FocusLost:Connect(function(enterPressed)
	local text = textBox.Text
	-- Only send if Enter was pressed and the box is not empty
	if enterPressed and #text > 0 then
		local success = pcall(function()
			return general:SendAsync(text)
		end)

		if not success then
			general:DisplaySystemMessage("Failed to send message")
		end

		-- Clear the box for the next message
		textBox.Text = ""
	end
end)
explain: `FocusLost` runs when the player stops typing. `enterPressed` is true if they pressed Enter.
`#text > 0` checks the message is not empty. `#` gives the length, so `#"hi"` is 2.
`SendAsync` sends the message. We wrap it in `pcall` so an error does not break the script.
If sending fails, we show a system message so the player knows.

watchOut: Forgetting to turn off the default chat window and input bar, so two chat boxes show at once.
Making a new label every time `MessageReceived` fires. Your own messages fire twice, so look up the label by `MessageId` first.
Using this with platform-integrated chat enabled. Message text comes back as an empty string, so the window shows nothing. Use `TextChannelWindow` instead.
